# [optional] generated by specgen

`include/beman/optional/optional.hpp` carries
[specgen](https://github.com/steve-downey/specgen) markup: `//!` comments on the
definitions, `// \rSec` section markers, and `// \ref` group headers in the class
bodies. This directory holds the wording specgen generates from the header, and
that wording marked against the C++ working draft.

| File | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `wording.tex` | the generated wording, draft LaTeX |
| `wording.md` | the same, mpark/wg21 markdown |
| `diff-vs-draft.tex`, `diff-vs-draft.md` | the generated wording marked against the working draft's [optional] |
| `specgen-version.txt` | the specgen that wrote them |
| `generate.sh` | regenerates all of the above |

The diff was taken against N5054, the `n5054` tag of cplusplus/draft
(`45b03900`). Removed text is the draft's, added text is this library's, so the
diff is also the list of places where the library and the draft disagree.

```sh
SPECGEN=/path/to/specgen DRAFT_SOURCE=/path/to/draft/source ./generate.sh
```

`generate.sh` runs `specgen generate --validate`, which reports nothing above a
note for the header.

## Where the wording comes from

A description is the draft's text where the implementation does what the draft
says. Where specgen can derive an element from the code it is derived: a
*Constraints* from a `requires`-clause, a *Mandates* from a `static_assert`, an
*Effects: Equivalent to* from a function body. Those are the elements that show
a difference when the implementation and the draft differ.

## Differences that come from the header's layout

- [optional.bad.access] comes before [optional.optional]: the class has to be
  complete before the member functions that throw it, and a section is where
  its class is defined. The diff shows the subclause as moved, not compared.
- *`converts-from-any-cvref`* is declared under [optional.optional], ahead of
  the class that uses it, where the draft introduces it in [optional.ctor].
- The header synopsis is gathered from the declarations, so the diff replaces
  the draft's synopsis whole instead of marking it line by line.
- `optional<T&>::optional(nullopt_t)` is defined in the class and has an item of
  its own; the draft defines it in the class synopsis and does not describe it.
